# NA19239_h2 / NA19240_h1 group81264 realignment regression

`na19239_na19240_group81264.json.gz` contains the three sequences and two original
query graph CIGARs supplied by the user on 2026-09-21. The reference graph path is
one 92,353-base `M` operation. Query sequences are in graph traversal orientation;
the father sequence is already reverse-complemented.

The supplied FASTAs include one more base than the graph's half-open coordinates:
reference 92,354 vs 92,353; both queries 93,505 vs 93,504. To match the graph
intervals, remove the first reference base and first child base. Remove the last
father base because its supplied sequence is reverse-complemented. Every original
graph-CIGAR I/X payload was checked against the adjusted query sequence. No
alignment or sequence correction is used to construct the fixture.

The owned query slice is [25,700, 67,542) in both oriented queries. These 41,842
bases are identical, ignoring letter case. Their different graph traversals
previously survived the whole-pair rescue because asm5 returned fragmented,
lower-scoring candidates. Default minimap2 mapping previously gave higher-scoring
candidates and matching SV calls under the +2/-3, `12 + 12*log2(n+1)` score.
With match +4 / mismatch -8 / gap `12 + 100*log2(n)`, the father's candidate
is rejected and the child's is accepted. With the same logarithmic score also
used for D/I repair, their final SV representations differ. With the separate
affine D/I repair score (+1/-4; gap `4 + (n - 1)`), downstream repair produces
matching SV calls on the identical owned slice with mappy 2.31. The CLI 2.31
backend still gives different repeat decompositions between father and child.

The real-data test runs the available mappy and executable backends independently.
It verifies one early mapper invocation per pair, the different acceptance
decisions, complete sequence spelling and valid reference bounds, and the
resulting backend-specific father/child SV call signatures. The backends can choose
different repeat decompositions. Sequence preservation and score improvement
are not assertions of consistent SV representation between relatives.

This fixture validates this locus, not whole-trio benchmark accuracy.
